label: May 4–10
title: “Rebel Not Ye against the Lord, Neither Fear” —  Numbers 11–14; 20

items.text: The 40 years the children of Israel spent in the wilderness were not about covering geographical distance, but spiritual distance—the distance between who they were and who they could become as God’s covenant people. These lessons prepare us for our promised land: eternal life with our Heavenly Father.

God guides His Church through His prophet, and while all can receive personal revelation, not all can lead God's people. Understanding personal revelation and the importance of following His prophet is crucial for our spiritual journey and preparedness.

Moses, the mighty leader who stood before Pharaoh and performed miracles, was also described as ‘very meek.’ Meekness is not weakness; it is strength under divine control, a willingness to submit to God’s will, and a deep trust in His power and love.

When faced with daunting challenges, the Israelites wanted to return to Egypt out of fear. However, Caleb and Joshua possessed a different spirit, one filled with faith in the Lord. Their example teaches us to apply faith to overcome our own fears and uncertainties.

Caleb and Joshua’s faith in the Lord empowered them to see the promised land as conquerable. Their unwavering trust in God’s promises and power stands as a testament to how faith can help us face any obstacle and achieve divine purposes.

The story of the brazen serpent illustrates that when we look to Jesus Christ in faith, He can heal us spiritually. The Book of Mormon prophets understood and taught this vital principle, reminding us to turn to the Savior for healing.

If I look to Jesus Christ in faith, He can heal me spiritually. The story of the brazen serpent serves as a powerful symbol of our need to focus on the Savior for spiritual healing and redemption from our sins and afflictions.

Understanding the lessons learned by the children of Israel in their spiritual wilderness can help us prepare to enter our own promised land. Their journey teaches us the consequences of faithlessness and the power of repentance and looking to the Savior.

The Lord’s power is evident even when the future seems hopeless. By learning to trust in His strength, we can overcome our own feelings of despair and move forward with faith, knowing He is with us through every trial.

Being faithful to the Lord's servants is a vital lesson from the Israelites' journey. This principle underscores the importance of respecting and following those whom the Lord has called to lead and guide His people.
